answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, where agents are assigned a unique digital identity, akin to a quill-penned signature. As agents participate in the network, their reputation grows, anchoring them to a virtual reef of trust. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to expend significant computational resources, akin to swimming against a rising tide of verification requirements, making it economically infeasible to launch a successful Sybil attack.
